answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a slashable identity bond: each agent locks a stake tied to a unique, attested key before it may vote. A verifiable random beacon picks an audit panel each epoch, so an attacker cannot know which hollow shells get checked. Even a sudden gale of fresh identities faces random audits, and any node caught double-signing or relaying forged attestations loses its whole bond, which is burned. The attacker pays N bonds up front plus expected slash loss, a cost that grows with every identity while one sparrow vote stays nearly weightless, so flooding never pays.
